ledger.note: 1208: Azzo VI d'Este becomes lord of Ferrara. 'In 1208, Azzo VI d'Este became seignior of Ferrara' (the page also says the territory was ruled by the House of Este 'from 1146 to 1597' and does not reconcile the two). Rovigo had been 'a formal possession of Azzo VI d'Este' since 1194 (Rovigo page).

ledger.note: 1482: Venice goes to war with Ferrara. 'The immediate casus belli at the beginning of 1482 was, as usual, a minor infraction of prerogatives'; Venetian troops overran Comacchio, sacked Adria, attacked Argenta and besieged Ficarolo and Rovigo.

wars.outcome: Venice took Rovigo (capitulated 17 August 1482) and besieged Ferrara from November 1482; the Treaty of Bagnolo (7 August 1484) left Venice 'the town of Rovigo and a broad swath of the fertile delta of the Po'.

wars.outcome: The Este recovered Rovigo during the war; Venice returned in 1514 and kept it to 1797. Julius II excommunicated Alfonso I in 1509; Alfonso beat the papal army at Ravenna in 1512.
wars.note: Only Ferrara's part is recorded; the war page was not opened and the years 1509-1514 are those of the Ferrara and Rovigo pages.

notes: Written from five pages. This dossier is Ferrara only. The House of Este also held Modena (from 1288) and Reggio (from 1289) and was Duke of Modena and Reggio from 1452 (Duchy of Ferrara page); those lands are the duchy-of-modena-and-reggio dossier (eu-20, Cliopatria row 1815-1859) and nobody has written the Este Modena of 1288-1814, which needs a gap-filler. The start year 1208 matches the Papal States ledger's vassal_start (eu-13-d); the page also says the Este ruled 'from 1146'. The Venice ledger (eu-13-c) uses duchy-of-ferrara for the Polesine of Rovigo and matches the events here, apart from its 1481 on the Venice page against 1482 on the Rovigo and war pages. Unsettled: the Polesine's holder in 1438-1481 and its extent (Rovigo province is a reading); when the Este took Comacchio; the year of the 1509 recovery of Rovigo (the Rovigo page is silent); the Ferrara page gives 1597 for the loss while the transfer to the pope came in 1598 (Cesare page: Modena entered January 1598). The pages for the League of Cambrai war and the 1598 Convention of Faenza were not opened. Gazetteer: no names needed (Comacchio is a coordinate).
